segments.title: 第107章 徐有漁的盟主
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Era Chapter 107: Xu Youyu's Alliance Lord

It was a rare occasion for Ying Zhicheng to return from his company to stay for two days, so Ying Chanxi and Li Luo didn't go back to Bihai Lanting on Friday and Saturday.

It wasn't until after lunch on Sunday that the two packed their school bags and returned to Bihai Lanting 1502, planning to rest for a bit.

Because Ying Chanxi had joined the math competition group, she also had to go to school for competition training on Sunday afternoon.

So right after returning to Bihai Lanting and eating a "Little Pudding" ice cream bar, she licked her lips, slung her school bag over her shoulder, told Li Luo she was leaving, and headed out for school.

As for Li Luo, he locked himself in his bedroom, turned on his computer, and quickly started writing to replenish the stockpile he had used up over the past two days.

After a grueling afternoon of writing over ten thousand words, Li Luo leaned back in his chair and took a slight breather.

Just then, his QQ avatar started flashing. Someone was looking for him.

Qian Zhou: The Online Writers' Association has already approved your application. Wait for their staff to give you a call to arrange a time to pick up the association's materials and certificate, and then you'll officially be a member.

Chong Ran: Okay, thank you, Editor.

Qian Zhou: The main purpose of the Online Writers' Association is to build a bridge for communication, including between authors, and between authors and officials.

Qian Zhou: If you have the opportunity and time, you can consider participating in some of the association's future activities. Getting to know more people will be beneficial for you down the line.

Chong Ran: I still have school, so I might not have that much time usually.

Qian Zhou: No worries, no worries, it was just a suggestion.

Qian Zhou: At the end of the day, connections are built on the foundation of your own strength.

Qian Zhou: So the most important thing for you right now, aside from school, is to maintain your updates and focus on writing this book well.

Qian Zhou: The entertainment genre is a major category for distribution channels. Once you reach one million words and get approved for distribution, your royalties from the channels should be no lower than what you get from the main site.

Chong Ran: Mm, I understand.

His current average subscriptions were just over three thousand, and the growth had stagnated. There would probably be a few more recommendations from the website later on.

Based on his experience from his previous life, it would at most rise to around four or five thousand average subscriptions.

But even so, for him at this moment, it was already a lot.

After all, based on his update volume, if this book could reach five thousand average subscriptions, his monthly royalties would be at least over 20,000 yuan.

In his past life, online literature had gradually entered the era of widespread anti-piracy measures.

Qidian authors' subscription income primarily came from paid subscriptions from readers on the main site.

But in the current year of 2014, distribution channels were all the rage.

Many online novel readers might not have known about Qidian, but they would search for all sorts of websites on the internet.

Some found free pirate sites and read with great relish.

But others didn't understand the difference between pirated and official versions and might have clicked into an official channel's website due to a promotional redirect.

These websites sourced their books from Qidian, importing a large number of relatively better-performing online novels in batches, and then guided users to pay.

The revenue earned was shared with Qidian and the original author according to their contract.

Websites like these had sprung up like bamboo shoots after a spring rain in recent years, forming the vast distribution system behind the Wenyue Group.

And when the era of mobile internet arrived, this prosperous scene was pushed to its peak.

Otherwise, relying solely on the traffic and readers from the main site during this period, income was indeed limited.

Don't be fooled by Li Luo's three-thousand-plus average subscriptions, which earned him over ten thousand a month.

In reality, in their urban genre's "Boutique" author group, excluding a few editors, there were only 27 members in total.

And this was for a major category like urban fiction.

For some of the less popular categories, the number of authors who could cross the 3,000 average subscription "Boutique" line would only be smaller.

Across the entirety of Qidian, the number of authors who had truly written a "Boutique" work was probably only one or two hundred.

All the other ordinary authors were just cannon fodder beneath the successful and famous.

If the top 1% of practitioners in an industry couldn't even meet a 10,000 yuan income threshold, then that industry was a bit too bleak.

As he thought this, Li Luo clicked open the comment section of his book again.

That post by Yan Zhusheng was still being bumped up from time to time.

And besides that, another very familiar ID had appeared in his comment section.

GoToBedEarlyAndYou'llGrowTaller: I really like Jiang Mingyue! Can Chong Ran-dada write more of Yueyue's plotlines!

Li Luo: "?"

Looking closely, Li Luo discovered that Xu Youyu had not only posted in his comment section but had also tipped him an Alliance Lord.

Posting with the Alliance Lord title, her post directly formed a factional rivalry with Yan Zhusheng's.

Those who liked Mo Qinghan would leave comments for Yan Zhusheng and bump her post.

Those who liked Jiang Mingyue would flock to Xu Youyu's side to post.

The battle was unprecedentedly fierce.

Li Luo hadn't paid much attention to the comment section for the past half month and was surprised to see it had evolved to this state, leaving him not knowing whether to laugh or cry.

He thought for a moment, then opened Xu Youyu's novel, *Wen Yi Nian Dai*, and tipped her an Alliance Lord, a simple gesture of returning the favor.

He also wrote a long review for her, praising her book with well-reasoned arguments, and posted it in her comment section.

Just as Li Luo finished posting the comment, he heard the sound of the front door opening outside his bedroom.

Li Luo got up and walked out of his room to see Xu Youyu walking in with her school bag, changing into slippers, and greeting him.

"Yo, you're back." Xu Youyu waved at Li Luo, then asked, "Where's Xixi?"

"She went to school for competition tutoring."

"Oh right, I forgot." Xu Youyu looked a little troubled as she held up a bag in her hand. "I bought quite a few groceries, I think I bought too much."

"If you bought too much, just put it in the fridge."

"That could work." Xu Youyu thought for a moment, then had a sudden flash of inspiration and suggested, "Or I could call Zhusheng and ask if she wants to come over for dinner, then we can go to school together."

"Oh..." Li Luo recalled how Yan Zhusheng had taken the initiative on Friday to tell the cooking auntie she wouldn't be home for dinner, so he nodded. "Go ahead and ask her then."

Hearing this, Xu Youyu immediately took out her phone and made the call.

"Want to come for dinner? Li Luo is cooking."

"Okay."

Three seconds after the call connected, Xu Youyu hung up and gave Li Luo an "okay" sign. "Alright, she's coming over now."

Li Luo: "...Why was that so fast?"

"What's wrong with being fast?" Xu Youyu shot him a look. "Since Xixi isn't here, do you need my help as a kitchen hand?"

"That won't be necessary." Li Luo shook his head. "I'm afraid you'll cut your fingers off."

"Underestimating me?" Xu Youyu's eyes widened. She had originally planned to be lazy, but now she had no choice but to charge into the kitchen. "I can at least wash vegetables, okay!"

"Fine, fine." With a helpless look, Li Luo took the apron Ying Chanxi usually wore from the wall and handed it to Xu Youyu. "Put this on first, don't splash water on yourself."

Unlike with Ying Chanxi, after Xu Youyu put on the apron, its hem only reached the top of her thighs.

Normally, when Ying Chanxi wore it, the hem reached her knees.

Li Luo subconsciously glanced a couple more times at such a magnificent sight, then suddenly remembered the teasing remark Xu Youyu had made in front of Yan Zhusheng before. He was instantly on alert and instinctively glanced at Xu Youyu's eyes.

Then he saw her half-smiling gaze.

"Ahem..." Li Luo guiltily averted his gaze and handed the vegetables that needed washing to Xu Youyu. "Just wash these."

"Oh." Xu Youyu nodded. While diligently washing the ingredients, she kindly shared her experience with him. "For girls, a guy's gaze is very easy to read."

"Especially for a girl like me who's been popular since she was little. Basically, whenever I go out, I can feel people's eyes on me."

"Over time, I can even subconsciously feel when someone is looking at me."

As she spoke, Xu Youyu might have felt her explanation wasn't vivid enough, so she said with a smile, "Next time I'm free, I'll take you out shopping."

"While walking on the street, don't look at anything else, just stare at the men passing by."

"Basically nine out of ten will look over."

"And the last one will be staring the whole time."

"I'm already used to it."

It had to be said, Xu Youyu had always had such a poised and generous personality, and she never shied away from these topics in conversation.

Li Luo had originally thought that the Xu Youyu from his past life had only slowly developed this personality after she matured with age.

He hadn't expected her to be like this even in high school.

"It's my nature, can't be helped," Li Luo sighed. "The first glance is instinct, I just look over subconsciously."

"What about the next few glances?" Xu Youyu raised an eyebrow.

"The next few glances are because everyone has a love for beauty."

"And the one who keeps staring?"

"Is a fair lady, a gentleman's good match."

"Haha, you silver-tongued devil." Xu Youyu laughed happily, the apron jiggling with her laughter.

She felt that being with Li Luo always made it easy to gather material, and it was always about things that other guys rarely talked about.

She had to find a way to write their recent conversation into her novel.

Hmm... she'd use it for the male and female leads.

The male lead glances a few more times at another girl, and the female lead pinches his ear. Amid their playful bickering, the male lead gives a witty response.

It sounded interesting just thinking about it.

Xu Youyu nodded in satisfaction, her vegetable-washing movements becoming a bit more diligent.

For the past month or two, her readers had been praising how the daily interaction scenes she wrote were getting more and more interesting, and the results were also quite good.

From an initial first-day subscription of just over 1,000, she had now reached over 1,800 average subscriptions. With a little more effort, she might even be able to touch the 2,000 mark.

She earned over five thousand in royalties last month!

Although it still wasn't as impressive as the guy next to her...

Xu Youyu glanced at Li Luo and huffed inwardly, secretly steeling herself, hoping for the day she could surpass him.

(End of Chapter)
